correctness.rationale: For \(L>0\), \(G\ge L/\sqrt2\), \(0<p<1\), an optimal center in the gap must draw strictly positive masses \(A=pu/L\), \(B=(1-p)v/L\) from both intervals. Exact uniform integrations give error \(L^2/12-S_L-S_R+T\). Since \(AB/(A+B)\ge\min(A,B)/2\) and the between-component mean difference is strictly larger than \(G\), the penalty satisfies \(T>\min(S_L,S_R)\). The remaining gain is at most \(L^2\max(p,1-p)/16\), which an explicit componentwise 2+1 codebook already achieves or improves. Thus a support-gap-support triple is strictly suboptimal at every boundary allowed. Exact rational tests and direct integration independently reproduce representative equalities but are not the infinite proof.

Its earlier examples concern isolated probabilities and do not imply the inequality for every weight. Published eventual-separation assertions concern large codebook sizes, not fixed three-point placement. Targeted terminology, full-text, and mathematical finding searches located no stronger claim, but an unindexed or older equivalent remains a residual risk.

value.rationale: Barua et al. explicitly asked whether their equally separated two-uniform mixture could have an optimal three-mean support-gap-support configuration while a two-mean gap point occurs. Showing the three-mean configuration impossible for every mixing weight answers that conjunction and reveals the reusable cross-variance-vs-splitting-gain obstruction for all equal-length intervals with sufficiently large gaps. This is a natural structural boundary, not an arbitrary finite parameter computation. The two-mean question alone and a sharp critical gap remain open.
